label: prf:markov-trace-product
title: Proof of markov trace product
html:
Write x_k = \rho(w_0 w_1 \cdots w_k), so that x_k \in H_{k+2}(R, q), the subalgebra generated by \sigma_0, \ldots, \sigma_k, and x_{-1} = 1. Then

  x_k = x_{k-1}\,(a_k \sigma_k + b_k),
  \qquad x_{k-1} \in H_{k+1}(R, q).

Since \sigma_k is the generator adjoined in passing from H_{k+1} to H_{k+2}, the Markov property \mathrm{tr}_M(x\,\sigma_k) = z\,\mathrm{tr}_M(x) for x \in H_{k+1} gives

  \mathrm{tr}_M(x_k)
  = a_k\, z\, \mathrm{tr}_M(x_{k-1}) + b_k\, \mathrm{tr}_M(x_{k-1})
  = (z\, a_k + b_k)\, \mathrm{tr}_M(x_{k-1}).

Induction from \mathrm{tr}_M(x_{-1}) = \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1 up to k = n-2 gives the product formula. A cyclic rotation of \beta has the same trace because \mathrm{tr}_M is a trace. \square

Scope: monotone words and their rotations only

The induction uses that every letter of \sigma_k lies to the right of every letter of \sigma_0, \ldots, \sigma_{k-1}. For a word in which generators interleave, grouping the letters by generator computes the trace of a different element, the monotone reordering.

  • \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 is a cyclic rotation of \sigma_0^2\sigma_1, so the formula holds: \hat V_0 \hat V_1 = (hz + 1)\,z = hz^2 + z, which is the corrected Markov trace (corrected Markov trace). Here h = q - q^{-1}, and \sigma_0^2 = h\sigma_0 + 1 gives a_0 = h, b_0 = 1. (Assigning the factor z to each crossing instead, giving z^3, is a different and incorrect rule.)
  • \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0\sigma_1 is not a rotation of a monotone word. The braid relation gives \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0\sigma_1 = \sigma_0^2\sigma_1\sigma_0 = h\,\sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 + \sigma_1\sigma_0, so \mathrm{tr}_M = h(hz^2 + z) + z^2, while the grouped product is (hz + 1)^2. The difference is z^2 - hz - 1 = -(q^4 + q^2 + 1)/(q^2 + 1)^2 \neq 0. The same value follows from the Wedderburn weights y_{(3)}, y_{(2,1)} and the seminormal (2,1) representation.
